title: Talos, Marex and Broadridge Plan After-Hours Financing for DTCC-Tokenized Treasuries
description: The three firms announced a November 17 collaboration linking Talos execution, Marex prime brokerage and Broadridge post-trade systems to finance tokenized U.S. Treasuries outside standard market hours.
why_it_matters: The proposed integration targets a practical obstacle in institutional tokenization: moving Treasury collateral into financing transactions while keeping brokerage records, interest calculations and settlement operations connected. The firms have announced plans, not completed commercial deployment.
keyTakeaways: Talos, Marex and Broadridge announced the planned integration on November 17, 2026.
The initial financing use case focuses on tokenized U.S. Treasuries using DTCC infrastructure.
Marex would provide prime brokerage, Talos execution connectivity and Broadridge DLX post-trade orchestration.
The companies have not demonstrated a live, integrated financing service or disclosed transaction volumes for this collaboration.
body:
Talos, Marex and Broadridge announced on November 17, 2026 that they intend to connect their systems to support institutional trading and financing of tokenized securities outside conventional market hours. The initial focus is financing tokenized U.S. Treasuries through the DTCC Tokenization Service. This is a proposed integration rather than an announcement that the combined financing workflow is already commercially operating.

Under the arrangement, Marex would provide prime brokerage services to financing clients. Talos would connect counterparties through its request-for-quote execution network. Broadridge would link those transactions to its DLX platform, coordinating on-chain settlement with conventional records, interest calculations and profit-and-loss reporting. The companies previously participated in DTCC production transactions in July 2026.

DTCC separately announced that its Tokenization Service launched on October 28, enabling eligible participants to create tokenized representations of securities held at DTC. The new collaboration seeks to build financing workflows on top of that infrastructure. Broadridge cited more than $350 billion in daily tokenized repo activity on its existing platform, but that figure must not be mistaken for activity generated by this new partnership.
